title: Robust Generation of Topological Biphoton Mode via Adiabatic Passage
authors: Jaesung Lim, Jihwan Kim, Dong-Gil Im, Kyungdeuk Park, Dongkyu Kim, Yonggi Jo, Yong Sup Ihn
abstract: Topological waveguide arrays support robust mode propagation in the presence of fabrication imperfections, providing a significant advantage for on-chip quantum information processing. However, this robustness does not fully extend to nonlinear biphoton generation. Structural disorder can enhance the excitation of non-topological biphoton modes during nonlinear interactions, which degrades the quantum properties of the generated state. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adiabatic passage that connects an isolated site to a topological defect array. By initiating the nonlinear process in a strongly isolated regime, nonlinear coupling to unwanted modes is effectively suppressed, thereby preserving the Schmidt number of the generated state. The subsequent adiabatic connection facilitates the high fidelity transfer of the generated biphoton into the topological biphoton mode. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that, unlike conventional topological structures, the adiabatic scheme maintains both high biphoton fidelity and a unit Schmidt number in the presence of waveguide gap disorder. Furthermore, we show that this robustness extends to path entangled NOON states, achieving a near-unity quantum interference visibility. Our approach provides a practical design strategy for disorder-tolerant integrated quantum photonic devices.
summary: The paper introduces an adiabatic passage technique to generate topological biphoton modes in waveguide arrays, overcoming the issue of structural disorder that plagues conventional methods. By first isolating the nonlinear process and then adiabatically transferring the state into the robust topological mode, the authors achieve high fidelity and unit Schmidt number even with significant disorder. This provides a practical design strategy for building reliable integrated quantum photonic devices.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving robust generation of topological biphoton modes for on-chip quantum processing, as structural disorder degrades the quantum state fidelity in conventional waveguide structures.
main_result: An adiabatic passage connecting an isolated site to a topological defect array maintains high biphoton fidelity and unit Schmidt number even with significant waveguide gap disorder. This method also preserves near-unity interference visibility for path entangled NOON states.
method: The authors propose using an adiabatic passage technique, initiating the nonlinear process in a strongly isolated regime before adiabatically transferring the generated state into the desired topological mode.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a one-dimensional silicon waveguide array supporting a Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) lattice. The dynamics are governed by coupled evolution equations for the pump and biphoton fields, incorporating nonlinear coupling via Spontaneous Four-Wave Mixing (SFWM).
key_observables: Biphoton fidelity ($|\langle T|\Psiangle|^2$), Schmidt number ($	ext{SN}$), quantum interference visibility ($V$), and spatial joint path intensity (JPI) distributions.
important_parameters: Waveguide gap disorder ($\delta$, up to 40 nm); pump wavelength (1550 nm); signal/idler wavelengths (1545 nm / 1555 nm).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that initiating the nonlinear process in a strongly isolated regime effectively suppresses unwanted coupling, and that the gap disorder preserves chiral symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the adiabatic connection (Fig. 1), eigenvalue spectrum separation confirming topological protection (Fig. 1b), spatial distributions comparing isolated vs. topological JPI under disorder (Fig. 3c/d), and performance comparisons for NOON states showing high visibility in the adiabatic case versus degradation in conventional arrays (Fig. 5).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of disorder-induced decoherence, introduces the SSH model and the concept of adiabatic passage, details the simulation methodology comparing adiabatic vs. conventional structures, demonstrates superior robustness for biphoton generation, and finally extends the findings to path entangled NOON states.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical limitations in integrated quantum photonics by providing a robust protocol (adiabatic passage) that leverages topological properties to maintain high-fidelity quantum state preparation despite realistic fabrication imperfections.

Fig. 3(b) presents the SN and fidelity of the output biphoton state. In the conventional topological array with central waveguide injection, the SN increases to 1.27 ± 0.293 while the fidelity drops to 0.826 ± 0.181 at the highest disorder strength. Even when the pump is launched into the topological mode, the SN still rises to 1.17 ± 0.221 and the fidelity degrades to 0.933 ± 0.074, accompanied by a relatively broad distribution. This confirms that biphoton generation in the conventional topological lattices is not fully resilient to disorder, con- sistent with a prior study [32].
